concepts.title: Phases of the Moon
concepts.definition: The Moon shines by reflected sunlight, and as it circles the earth we see changing lit portions called phases - new moon to crescent, first quarter, gibbous, full moon and back; the whole cycle from one new moon to the next takes about 29.5 days.
concepts.key_idea: The Moon never changes shape - only the sunlight portion visible from earth does, cycling in about 29.5 days.
concepts.textbook_ref: hecu111.txt lines 40-200 (moon's appearance, phases, waxing and waning)
question_patterns: why does the moon change its shape every night
name the phases of the moon in order
how long does one cycle of moon phases take
what is the difference between waxing and waning moon
why do we not see the moon on a new moon day
how does a ball-and-stick model explain the phases of the moon

solution_steps.explain: The Moon reflects sunlight; half its surface stays lit.
As the Moon orbits, the visible lit fraction grows and shrinks, creating the phases.
One full run of phases, new moon to new moon, needs about 29.5 days.

concepts.title: Eclipses
concepts.definition: When the earth comes between the sun and the moon, the earth's shadow darkens the moon - a lunar eclipse; when the moon slips between the sun and the earth, its shadow falls on the earth - a solar eclipse; eclipses are rare because the moon's tilted orbit rarely lines all three up.
concepts.key_idea: Eclipses are shadow games of the sun-earth-moon lineup.
question_patterns: what is a lunar eclipse and when does it occur
how is a solar eclipse different from a lunar eclipse
why do eclipses not happen every month
draw the arrangement of the sun, moon and earth for a solar eclipse
is it safe to watch a solar eclipse directly - what care is needed
why does the moon turn reddish during some lunar eclipses

solution_steps.explain: Sun, earth and moon must line up nearly straight for any eclipse.
Moon in earth's shadow gives a lunar eclipse; earth in moon's shadow gives a solar eclipse.
The moon's orbital tilt keeps it out of line most months.

concepts.title: Calendars from the Skies: Lunar and Solar Years
concepts.definition: Time-keeping grew from the sky: the day is the shortest natural unit, a lunar month runs about 29.5 days from new moon to new moon, twelve such months make a lunar year of 354 days, while the cycle of seasons - one trip of the earth around the sun - fixes the solar year of about 365 days.
concepts.key_idea: 12 lunar months of 29.5 days give a 354-day lunar year, 11 days short of the 365-day solar year.
concepts.textbook_ref: hecu111.txt lines 473-600 (how calendars came into existence, lunar calendars)
question_patterns: find the length of a lunar year with 12 lunar months of 29.5 days
by how many days is the lunar year shorter than the solar year
how did ancient people build calendars from the moon
what is a solar year and what causes the seasons
why do lunar calendar months drift across seasons
define a lunar month using the phases of the moon

solution_steps.explain: 12 lunar months of 29.5 days make the lunar year.
Subtracting the lunar year from the 365-day solar year gives the yearly gap.

concepts.title: Festivals and Astronomy
concepts.definition: Many Indian festivals are tied to sky events: Diwali falls on the new-moon night, Guru Nanak Jayanti and Buddha Purnima on full-moon days, and harvest festivals like Makar Sankranti mark the sun's northward journey - astronomy lives inside the calendar of celebrations.
concepts.key_idea: Festivals encode lunar phases and solar positions on the calendar.
concepts.textbook_ref: hecu111.txt lines 966-1050 (are festivals related to astronomical events)
question_patterns: which festivals fall on full moon days
on which phase of the moon is Diwali celebrated
how is Makar Sankranti connected to the sun's motion
name two festivals linked to lunar phases
why did ancient people tie festivals to the sky
find the moon phase on which a given festival occurs

solution_steps.explain: Look up whether the date follows the lunar tithi or the solar sankranti.
Full moon, new moon or solar transit decides the day.
The festival calendar mirrors the astronomical calendar.

concepts.title: Artificial Satellites
concepts.definition: Artificial satellites are human-made objects launched to circle the earth, serving communication, weather watching, navigation and research; placed at the right height and speed, they keep moving like the moon under gravity's grip.
concepts.key_idea: A satellite is a controlled moon: gravity bends its motion into a closed orbit.
concepts.textbook_ref: hecu111.txt lines 1050-1120 (why do we launch artificial satellites)
question_patterns: what is an artificial satellite - name two Indian satellites
why do satellites not fall back to the earth
list the uses of artificial satellites
how does a satellite stay in its orbit
what keeps the moon revolving around the earth
how do satellites help in weather forecasting

solution_steps.explain: A rocket lifts the satellite above the atmosphere with enough sideways speed.
Earth's pull curves the path into a circle or ellipse, so the satellite keeps falling around the planet.
TV signals, GPS, weather images and scientific data all arrive from orbit.
